A builder is a tool criminals or testers use to generate a customized malware file or payload.
BunnyCDN product
BunnyCDN is a legitimate content delivery network that helps websites distribute content from internet servers.
also: BunnyCDN [.b-cdn[.]net]
business-email-compromise technique
Business email compromise is a scam where attackers use or impersonate business email accounts to trick people into sending money or data.
Bypass technique
A bypass is a way to get around a security check, restriction, or protection.
C2 concept
C2, short for command and control, is the system attackers use to send instructions to compromised devices or malware.
C2 Servers concept
C2 servers are attacker-controlled computers that send commands to and receive data from infected devices.
CACTUS malware
CACTUS is a ransomware operation that encrypts victims' files and demands payment to restore access.
CACTUS Ransomware malware
CACTUS ransomware is malware that encrypts files and demands payment from victims to restore access.
CAIRN tool
CAIRN is an open-source research toolkit for finding and analyzing malware connected to AI systems.
also: Cairn attack search engine
canada
Canada is a North American country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
canary concept
A canary is a deliberately placed marker or trap used to reveal when something has been accessed, copied, or tampered with.
capture concept
A capture is a part of a regular expression that saves matched text so it can be reused or referenced later.
cargo
Cargo is Rust’s package manager and build tool.
censys tool
Censys is an internet scanning and search platform used to discover exposed systems and certificates.
Central Information Technology Center organization
The Central Information Technology Center is a government organization that operates and maintains important digital public services.
CERT-In organization
CERT-In is India’s national computer emergency response team for handling cybersecurity incidents and advisories.
also: CERT-In's finance team
certificate authorities organization
Certificate authorities are trusted organizations that issue digital certificates used to prove websites and services are legitimate.
Certificate Authority concept
A trusted organization or service that issues and signs digital certificates.
Certificate Revocation List protocol
A Certificate Revocation List is a list of digital certificates that should no longer be trusted.
Certificate Revocation Lists concept
Lists published by certificate authorities to tell software which digital certificates should no longer be trusted.
certificate transparency concept
Certificate transparency is a system of public logs that lets people check which website certificates have been issued.
Certighost vulnerability
Certighost is a named security-related tool, malware, or campaign referenced in reporting.
chat transcripts concept
Written records of messages exchanged in an online chat.
chatgpt
ChatGPT is OpenAI’s conversational AI assistant.
Check Point organization
Check Point is a cybersecurity company known for firewall, network security, and threat prevention products.
china
China is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving technology, espionage, regulation, and threat activity.
China-linked concept
China-linked describes activity, groups, or infrastructure believed to have some connection to China.
China-linked espionage concept
China-linked espionage refers to suspected spying activity connected to Chinese state interests or groups believed to work for them.
Chinese-speaking threat actor threat-actor
A Chinese-speaking threat actor is an attacker or group described as using Chinese language or infrastructure clues in security reporting.
Chrome product
A popular web browser developed by Google, frequently targeted by exploit kits and phishing campaigns.
Chrome Extension Sideloading technique
Chrome extension sideloading is installing a browser extension from outside the normal Chrome Web Store process.
CI concept
A software development practice where code changes are regularly merged and tested automatically.
CI pipelines concept
CI pipelines are automated steps that build and test code whenever developers make changes.
CI runner tool
A CI runner is a computer or service that automatically runs build, test, or deployment jobs for software projects.
CI runners concept
Programs that execute automated build and test jobs in a continuous integration pipeline, often on a server or cloud.
CI/CD concept
CI/CD is a software delivery approach that automatically builds, tests, and deploys code changes.
cisa organization
CISA is the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which helps protect critical infrastructure and shares security guidance.
also: U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog organization
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog is a U.S. government list of security flaws that attackers are known to be using in the real world.
Cisco organization
Cisco is a major technology company that makes networking hardware, security products, and communications systems.
Cisco BroadWorks product
Cisco BroadWorks is a communications platform used by service providers to deliver phone, messaging, and collaboration services.
Cisco Secure Firewall product
Cisco Secure Firewall is Cisco’s firewall product line for monitoring and blocking unwanted network traffic.
cisco-talos
Cisco Talos is Cisco’s threat intelligence and security research group.
also: Talos
Citrus Ransomware threat-actor
Citrus Ransomware is a threat-actor group associated with breaking into organizations, stealing data, and deploying ransomware.
also: Citrus, Citrus group
Claroc organization
Claroc is a security company referenced in security reporting.
claude
Claude is Anthropic’s family of AI assistants and language models.
Claude Opus 5.5 product
An Anthropic artificial-intelligence model designed to generate and analyze text.
claude-code
Claude Code is Anthropic’s AI coding assistant for helping developers write and manage software projects.
clickfix
ClickFix is a social-engineering tactic that tricks users into copying and running malicious commands to “fix” a fake problem.
also: ClickFix attacks
Client secrets concept
Client secrets are passwords or keys that an application uses to prove its identity when signing in to a service.
client services concept
Client services are programs or business functions that provide services directly to users or customer systems.
Client-side concept
Client-side refers to code or activity that runs on a user’s device or browser rather than on a server.
Clipboard Contents concept
Clipboard contents are the text, files, or other data a person has copied and may later paste.
clipboard data concept
Clipboard data is the text, images, or other content temporarily stored when a user copies or cuts something on a computer or phone.
Cloaking technique
A technique that shows different web content to different visitors, often hiding malicious pages from security checks.
cloning technique
Cloning is copying something, such as a code repository or system image, so the copy can be used elsewhere.
cloud concept
The cloud is internet-based computing where data and applications run on remote servers instead of only on your own device.
Cloud accounts concept
Cloud accounts are identities or subscriptions used to access services hosted by providers like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
cloud control plane concept
The cloud control plane is the management layer used to create, configure, and control cloud resources like servers, accounts, and storage.
Cloud credentials concept
Cloud credentials are passwords, keys, or tokens used to access cloud services and resources.
cloud environments concept
Cloud environments are computing systems and services run in cloud platforms rather than on local machines.
Cloud Identities concept
User accounts, service accounts, and roles that can access resources in a cloud environment.
cloud infrastructure concept
Cloud infrastructure is computing infrastructure provided through internet-based services.
cloud keys concept
Digital credentials used to access cloud accounts, services, or resources.
also: cloud key
Cloud misconfigurations concept
Incorrect cloud-service settings that can expose data, systems, or permissions.
Cloud Platform concept
An online service that provides computing, storage, or applications through the internet.
Cloud proxies tool
Cloud proxies are cloud-hosted services that relay, filter, or inspect traffic between users and online services.
Cloud Security Groups concept
Cloud security groups are cloud firewall rule sets that control which network traffic can reach virtual resources.
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
cloud-hosted concept
Stored or run on internet-connected provider infrastructure instead of directly on a local device.
CloudFront product
Amazon's content delivery network service, used to deliver websites and online content from nearby servers.
also: CloudFront host
Code 10 concept
A Windows Device Manager error indicating that a hardware device could not start.
also: This device cannot start (Code 10).
Code 10 errors concept
Windows Device Manager errors indicating that a hardware device cannot start.
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
Code repositories concept
Code repositories are storage locations where software source code and its change history are kept.
Code signing certificates concept
Code signing certificates are digital certificates used to sign software so users and systems can verify who published it and whether it was changed.
Codex CLI tool
Codex CLI is a command-line tool associated with OpenAI’s coding assistant capabilities.
Collaboration concept
Collaboration means people or organizations working together, often by sharing information, systems, or responsibilities.
command execution technique
Command execution means making a computer or device run instructions, often through a shell or remote interface.
command-and-control concept
Command-and-control is the way attackers remotely send instructions to malware and receive data back from infected machines.
Command-and-control server concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
also: C2 server
Command-and-control traffic technique
Command-and-control traffic is communication between malware on a victim system and the attacker’s server.
Commercial Cyber Intrusion Capabilities concept
Commercial cyber intrusion capabilities are tools and services sold to customers for breaking into, monitoring, or extracting data from digital systems.
commercial spyware malware
Commercial spyware is surveillance software sold by companies and used to secretly monitor devices or people.
Commitment technique
A cryptographic value that locks in information for later verification without revealing the information itself.
commits concept
Commits are saved sets of changes to files in a source-code repository.
compromise concept
A compromise is a situation where a system, account, or data has been breached or taken over by an attacker.
Compromise Campaign concept
A coordinated set of attacks intended to gain unauthorized access to many systems or victims.
compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised build concept
A compromised build is software that was tampered with during the build process before users received it.
compromised credentials concept
Compromised credentials are login details that have been stolen, exposed, or otherwise made unsafe.
Compromised devices concept
Compromised devices are computers, phones, or systems that attackers have gained unauthorized control over.
compromised endpoints concept
Computers, phones, servers, or other connected devices that an attacker has successfully breached.
Compromised Packages concept
Compromised packages are software packages that have been altered, hijacked, or published by an attacker and may harm users who install them.
compromised website concept
A legitimate site that has been hacked and may host malicious content or redirect visitors to phishing pages.
Computing Resources concept
The processing power, memory, storage, and network capacity used to run digital services.
Confiant organization
Confiant is a cybersecurity company that helps detect and stop malicious or deceptive online advertisements.
Confidential data concept
Confidential data is sensitive information that should only be seen by authorized people.
confidentiality, integrity, and availability concept
Confidentiality, integrity, and availability are the three basic goals of security: keeping data private, correct, and accessible when needed.
configuration data concept
Configuration data is the stored settings that tell software or systems how to behave.
Configuration Discovery technique
Configuration discovery is the process of finding a system's settings, services, accounts, and other operational details.
Configuration drift concept
Configuration drift happens when systems slowly change from their intended settings over time, creating security or reliability risks.
configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.
configuration information concept
Settings and parameters that determine how software or a device behaves.
Confirmed Breach concept
A verified incident in which an unauthorized party accessed, stole, exposed, or altered protected information or systems.
connected devices concept
Connected devices are everyday or business devices that can communicate over a network or the internet, such as phones, cameras, sensors, or appliances.
Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
Connection throttling technique
Connection throttling deliberately slows or limits network connections to reduce abuse, overload, or suspicious activity.
connection_established concept
A log event type indicating that a network connection was successfully made.
ConnectWise organization
ConnectWise is a software vendor known for remote management and IT service provider tools.
ConnectWise ScreenConnect product
ConnectWise ScreenConnect is a remote access and support product used to connect to and control computers over the internet.
Console product
A web-based control interface used to manage services, settings, and resources.
Constella Intelligence organization
A cybersecurity intelligence company that researches identity exposure and digital risks.
Contact Details concept
Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
Contact information concept
Contact information means details like an email address, phone number, or mailing address that can be used to reach someone.
container deployment token concept
A secret credential that allows software to deploy or manage applications packaged in containers.
Content Delivery Network concept
A Content Delivery Network is a group of servers that deliver websites and files faster by serving them from locations near users.
also: CDN
content filters tool
Content filters are controls that block, allow, or flag information based on rules about what the content contains.
Contractor concept
A person or company hired to perform work for an organization without being its regular employee.
Contractors concept
Contractors are outside workers or companies hired to perform work for another organization.
cookie concept
A cookie is a small piece of data a website stores in a browser to remember things like logins, preferences, or tracking information.
cookies concept
Cookies are small pieces of data websites store in a browser to remember logins, settings, or tracking information.
cooldown concept
A cooldown is a waiting period before something can happen again.
coordination concept
Coordination is the organized sharing of tasks, information, and decisions among people or teams.
Corporate credentials concept
Corporate credentials are work login details, such as usernames, passwords, or access tokens, used to access company systems.
corporate email accounts concept
Corporate email accounts are work email accounts provided by an organization to its employees or teams.
Corporate VPNs concept
Virtual private networks that let employees securely connect to an organization's internal systems remotely.
Crafty Falcon threat-actor
Crafty Falcon is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
also: CRAFTY FALCON campaign, "AI-assisted financial threat actor"
credential concept
A credential is proof of identity for logging in, such as a password, security token, API key, or certificate.
Credential Disclosure concept
Credential disclosure is the accidental or unauthorized exposure of login information such as usernames, passwords, or access tokens.
credential records concept
Credential records are stored details related to logins, such as usernames, passwords, tokens, or authentication metadata.
credential validation technique
Credential validation is the process of checking whether a username, password, token, or other login secret is valid.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
credit and identity monitoring concept
A service that watches for signs of suspicious credit activity or misuse of a person's identity.
also: Experian credit and identity monitoring
Critical concept
Critical is a severity rating meaning a vulnerability or incident could cause very serious damage and needs urgent attention.
critical issues concept
Critical issues are problems considered urgent because they can cause major harm, such as system compromise or serious service disruption.
Critical services concept
Critical services are essential systems or functions whose failure would seriously harm operations or public services.
critical vulnerabilities vulnerability
Critical vulnerabilities are very serious security flaws that could let attackers cause major damage or gain major access.
Critical vulnerability vulnerability
A critical vulnerability is a very serious security flaw that can cause major damage if exploited.
crowdstrike organization
CrowdStrike is a cybersecurity company known for endpoint protection, threat intelligence, and incident response.
crypto platforms product
Crypto platforms are services or systems for buying, selling, storing, or using cryptocurrency and digital assets.
also: crypto exchanges
Crypto4A organization
Crypto4A is a vendor of hardware security modules used to protect cryptographic keys.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
cryptocurrency exchanges organization
Cryptocurrency exchanges are online services where people buy, sell, or trade digital currencies like Bitcoin.
cryptocurrency payments concept
Cryptocurrency payments are transfers of digital currency such as Bitcoin or Ethereum instead of traditional money.
CSIRT-Fin organization
CSIRT-Fin is a financial-sector incident response team associated with India's CERT-In.
Cumulative updates concept
Cumulative updates are software updates that include current fixes plus earlier fixes in one package.
Customer and Partner Systems concept
Customer and partner systems are the computer systems operated by an organization's customers, suppliers, or other business associates.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer databases concept
Databases that store information about an organization's customers.
Customer endpoints concept
Customer endpoints are user devices or systems, such as laptops or servers, that belong to or serve customers.
Customer environments concept
Customer environments are the computers, cloud services, networks, and settings used by an organization.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
Customer Records concept
Stored information about customers, such as names, account details, and contact information.
Customer Vetting concept
Customer vetting is the process of checking a customer's identity, background, and intended use before providing a product or service.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
also: CVE records, CVE Program, CVE number
CVE identifier concept
A CVE identifier is the standard public tracking number assigned to a known cybersecurity vulnerability.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS concept
CVSS is a standard scoring system used to rate how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS 9.8 concept
A very high severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale.
CVSS base score concept
A CVSS base score is a number from 0 to 10 that summarizes how severe a security vulnerability is.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS score of 9.8 concept
A very high rating on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, indicating a critical security flaw.
CVSS v3.1 Score concept
A standardized numerical rating used to show how severe a software vulnerability is likely to be.
CVSS v4 concept
CVSS v4 is a standard system for assigning a severity score to a security vulnerability.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber intrusion concept
A cyber intrusion is an unauthorized break-in or access attempt against computers, accounts, or networks.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
CyberStrikeAI tool
An open-source framework referenced in security reporting that uses a language model to help direct actions on compromised systems.
CyCognito organization
CyCognito is a cybersecurity company known for external attack surface management technology.
Cynet organization
Cynet is a cybersecurity company that provides threat detection and response products and services.
D-Shortiez threat-actor
D-Shortiez is a threat actor associated with forced redirects, phishing, and tech-support scam campaigns.
also: China-based forced-redirect actor
Daily Cyber Headlines product
A recurring news resource that summarizes cybersecurity headlines.
dashboard tool
A dashboard is a visual interface where users manage settings and view information in a product.
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
also: the incident, potential cybersecurity incident, the exposure
data centers concept
Data centers are facilities full of servers and networking equipment that run websites, cloud services, and business systems.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data files concept
Data files are computer files that store information, such as records, documents, logs, or exported databases.
Data Flows concept
The paths data takes as it moves between people, applications, devices, and services.
data loss concept
The accidental or unauthorized destruction, exposure, theft, or unavailability of data.
Data retention concept
Data retention means how long an organization keeps information before deleting or archiving it.
Data Sources concept
Data sources are systems, services, or devices from which information is collected.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
Database Connection Strings concept
Settings that tell an application how to connect to a database, sometimes including sensitive login details.
Database credentials concept
Database credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used to access a database.
Dataset concept
A dataset is an organized collection of information used for analysis, reporting, or training software.
decoys technique
Decoys are fake targets, files, accounts, or systems used to distract attackers or detect suspicious behavior.
Decrypt technique
Decrypt is a cryptographic operation that turns encrypted data back into readable data when the correct key is used.
decryption concept
Decryption is the process of turning scrambled encrypted data back into readable information.
DeepAudit tool
DeepAudit is a security tool or project name referenced in security reporting.
DeepSeek organization
DeepSeek is an AI service provider referenced in the article.
DeepSeek Flash product
DeepSeek Flash is an artificial intelligence model or service offered under the DeepSeek name.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Defused organization
Defused is the threat intelligence company named in the article.
Delegation concept
Delegation is the act of giving another account, service, or smart contract permission to perform actions on one's behalf.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
denmark other
Denmark is a country in Northern Europe.
dependents concept
Dependents are people, such as family members, who are covered under another person's benefits or records.
deserialization technique
The process of converting data from a stored format back into a runtime object, a common target for injection attacks.
also: deserialization flaws
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection rules concept
Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
detector tool
A detector is a security rule, model, or tool that looks for signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
Dev Machine Guard tool
Dev Machine Guard is a security tool or product name referenced in reporting.
Developer machine concept
A developer machine is a computer used by a software developer to write, build, test, or release code, making it a valuable target for attackers.
Developer machines concept
Developer machines are computers used by software developers to write, build, and test code.
Developer Platform product
Cloudflare's environment for building and operating developer applications and services.
Developer Tools product
Developer Tools are software features and applications that help programmers create, test, and troubleshoot software.
Development environment concept
The computers, services, and tools used to create, test, and improve software.
Device Manager tool
Device Manager is a Windows tool for viewing and managing hardware devices and drivers.
DevOps concept
DevOps is a way of working where software development and IT operations teams collaborate to build, deploy, and run software faster.
DGA technique
A domain generation algorithm is a technique malware uses to create many possible website names so attackers can keep finding a working command server.
also: DGA shape
DHCP protocol
DHCP is a network protocol that automatically gives devices settings such as IP addresses and gateways.
DHCP server protocol
A DHCP server automatically gives devices network settings such as IP addresses when they join a network.
DHCP Server Role product
The DHCP Server role is a Windows Server feature that assigns network settings, such as IP addresses, to devices.
Digital Breadcrumbs concept
Traces of activity, such as logs and records, that people and programs leave behind on digital systems.
also: digital diary entries, fingerprints
digital certificates concept
Digital certificates are electronic credentials that help prove a website, device, or user is who they claim to be.
Digital identity concept
Digital identity is the online information and credentials that represent a person, device, or organization.
digital services concept
Digital services are online or computer-based services such as websites, apps, portals, and cloud systems.
Dirac Audio Improvement Software product
Audio-processing software that enhances sound on some Windows computers.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
Display name concept
A display name is the human-readable name shown for an account, sender, or object, which may differ from its real identifier.
display name impersonation technique
Display name impersonation is when an attacker makes an email sender name look like a trusted person even though the actual address is different.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
distinct() technique
A data-processing operation that removes duplicate entries from a dataset.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
also: DKIM signature, DKIM pass
DLL sideloading technique
DLL sideloading is an attack where malware places a fake DLL where a trusted Windows program will load it.

DLP, or data loss prevention, is technology that helps stop sensitive information from being leaked or sent where it should not go.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
also: DMARC policy, dmarc=fail
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
DNS lookup concept
A DNS lookup is the process of asking the Domain Name System to find the internet address for a domain name.
docker
Docker is a platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
Docker Image product
A Docker image is a packaged snapshot of an application and everything it needs to run in a container.
domain controller concept
A domain controller is a server that manages logins, permissions, and identity for a Windows network domain.
also: DC01, DC02, DC03
domain controllers product
Domain controllers are servers that manage logins, permissions, and security policies in a Windows domain.
Domain-Reputation Systems concept
Domain-reputation systems assess whether an internet domain appears trustworthy or associated with harmful activity.
dormant-neuron reprogramming technique
Dormant-neuron reprogramming is a technique that changes rarely used parts of an AI model so they activate only under selected conditions.
download page concept
A download page is a web page where users can obtain software, files, or updates.
DreamHost organization
A web-hosting company that provides website, domain, email, and server services.
driver records concept
Government records containing information about a person's driver license, driving history, or related vehicle details.
drones concept
Aircraft that can fly without a person onboard, often controlled remotely or autonomously.
also: a drone
DSPs concept
Demand-side platforms, or DSPs, are advertising systems that automatically buy digital ad placements for advertisers.
also: buying platforms
early warning concept
Early warning is advance notice of possible cyber danger before it becomes a confirmed or damaging incident.
eBPF concept
eBPF is a Linux technology that lets small programs run inside the operating system kernel for monitoring, networking, or security tasks.
ebpfkit tool
ebpfkit is an offensive eBPF project that demonstrates how eBPF can be used to alter or hide Linux system behavior.
EC2 product
Amazon EC2 is Amazon Web Services’ cloud service for renting virtual servers.
ECDSA protocol
ECDSA is a digital-signature algorithm used to prove that data came from the expected sender and was not changed.
ECS product
ECS commonly refers to Amazon Elastic Container Service, an AWS product for running and managing containerized applications.
EDI protocol
EDI, or electronic data interchange, is a standard way for businesses to exchange documents such as orders and invoices electronically.
EDR product
EDR is security software that monitors computers and servers for suspicious activity and helps respond to attacks.
EKS product
EKS, or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service, is AWS's managed service for running Kubernetes clusters.
elevation of privilege technique
Elevation of privilege is when someone gains higher access rights than they should have, such as becoming an administrator.
also: elevation of privilege vulnerability
email access concept
Email access means the ability to read, send, or manage someone’s email account, which attackers often want because it can unlock other services.
Email security concept
Email security protects inboxes and users from threats such as phishing, malware, and scam messages.
email systems concept
Email systems are the services and software that send, receive, store, and manage email messages.
Employee credentials concept
Employee credentials are usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login details used by workers.
employee data concept
Employee data is information an organization keeps about its workers, such as names, contact details, job records, or payroll information.
emSign product
emSign is a digital certificate and trust-services brand operated by eMudhra.
eMudhra organization
An Indian digital-trust company that issues certificates used to verify identities and secure online connections.
eMudhra Certificates product
eMudhra Certificates are digital certificates issued through eMudhra that can be used to verify identities or sign software and documents.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
End of support concept
End of support means a product has reached the date when its maker stops providing regular fixes, help, or security updates.
end-to-end encrypted concept
End-to-end encrypted means only the sender and intended recipient can read the message, not the service provider carrying it.
end-to-end encryption concept
End-to-end encryption protects messages so only the sender and intended recipient can read them.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
Endpoint agents tool
Endpoint agents are small programs installed on devices to monitor, manage, or protect them.
Endpoint Lookup Calls protocol
Requests to the Microsoft Endpoint Mapper service to find the network location of another service.
Endpoint Mapper protocol
A Microsoft RPC service that tells programs which network port a requested service is using.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
ENISA organization
ENISA is the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, which supports cybersecurity policy, guidance, and coordination across Europe.
Enterprise Policy concept
An enterprise policy is a set of rules an organization uses to control what users and systems are allowed to do.
Entity Redaction technique
Entity redaction hides sensitive details such as names, account numbers, or addresses by replacing them with safe placeholders.
Entra product
Microsoft Entra is Microsoft’s identity and access management product family, including cloud directory and login services.
Entra Device Registration product
Entra Device Registration is a Microsoft identity service feature that registers devices so an organization can manage their access.
enumerate technique
To enumerate means to systematically list or discover items such as users, devices, services, or files during security testing.
envelope sender protocol
The envelope sender is the technical return address used during email delivery, which may differ from the visible From address.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.
EpmapSavedContextCap other
A Windows Registry setting that controls a resource limit for the Microsoft Endpoint Mapper service.
ePUAP product

Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged access concept
Privileged access is a higher level of permission that lets a user or system make important changes or view sensitive information.
Privileged accounts concept
Privileged accounts are user or service accounts with powerful permissions that can make major changes to systems or data.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
Probe technique
A probe is an attempt to test a system for weaknesses or useful information before an attack.
Probes technique
Automated checks sent to systems to discover services, versions, or possible vulnerabilities.
Process Name concept
A process name is the name of a program currently running on a computer.
also: processes
Product UI Does Not Warn User of Unsafe Actions concept
Product UI Does Not Warn User of Unsafe Actions is a software weakness where an application fails to alert people before they take a risky action.
production concept
Production is the live environment where real users and real data are handled.
also: production access, UAT-to-production access
Production Credentials concept
Secret login details that provide access to live systems used by real customers or organizations.
Production environments concept
Production environments are the live systems that real users depend on, as opposed to test or development systems.
ProjectDiscovery organization
ProjectDiscovery is a company and open-source project that makes tools for finding security weaknesses in internet-facing systems.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompting technique
Prompting is the practice of giving instructions and information to an AI model to guide its response.
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
Proof-of-Concept Code concept
Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
also: PoC
proof-of-concept exploits tool
Proof-of-concept exploits are example programs or instructions that show a security flaw can be used in practice.
Propaganda concept
Propaganda is information spread to influence people's beliefs or actions, often in a one-sided or misleading way.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
PseudoCamo threat-actor
PseudoCamo is a named scam cluster that uses cloaked webpages and app-building platforms to host deceptive investment pages.
also: cloaked investment-scam cluster
Public disclosure concept
Public disclosure is the act of making information, such as a security flaw, available to the public.
public models concept
Public models are AI models that are available for broad outside use, often through websites, apps, or cloud services.
Public package registries concept
Public online services where developers publish and download reusable software packages.
Public preview concept
A public preview is an early version of a product or feature made available for people to test before final release.
Public proof-of-concept exploits tool
Public proof-of-concept exploits are publicly shared demonstration code or instructions showing how a vulnerability can be attacked.
Public registries concept
Public registries are open online repositories where people publish and download software packages, container images, or other shared components.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
Publicly disclosed concept
Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
Publish concept
Publish means making an application, webpage, or other content available for other people to access online.
push technique
A push is the act of sending local code changes to a remote source-code repository such as GitHub.
pypi
PyPI is the main public package repository for Python software libraries.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
Python script tool
A Python script is a small program written in the Python programming language.
Qlik organization
Qlik is a software company known for business intelligence, analytics, and data integration products.
Qlik Sense product
Qlik Sense is a business analytics and data-visualization product made by Qlik.
quarantine technique
Quarantine is a holding area where suspicious files or emails are isolated so they cannot cause harm right away.
Qwen product
Qwen is a family of large language and AI models developed by Alibaba.
Qwen3.6-27B product
An open-weight AI language model that people can download, inspect, and adapt for their own uses.
Radioactive Material concept
Radioactive material is a substance that emits radiation and may be harmful if it is not handled safely.
also: hazardous material
Rails product
Rails, also called Ruby on Rails, is a popular web application framework used to build websites and web services.
Railway product
Railway is a cloud hosting platform used to deploy applications and services.
ransom concept
A sum of money demanded by criminals to restore access to data or systems after a ransomware attack.
ransom notes concept
Ransom notes are messages from attackers demanding payment, usually after data has been encrypted or stolen.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
also: ransomware attacks, ransomware campaigns
Ransomware deployment technique
Ransomware deployment is the stage where attackers install or run ransomware on victim systems.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
ransomware groups threat-actor
Ransomware groups are criminal teams that use ransomware or data theft to extort victims for money.
ransomware-as-a-service concept
Ransomware-as-a-service is a criminal business model where ransomware developers rent their malware to other attackers.
also: RaaS platform Sn00py
RDP protocol
RDP is Microsoft’s Remote Desktop Protocol, which lets someone control a Windows computer over a network.
also: internet-facing terminal servers over RDP
Read-Only concept
A permission setting that allows someone to view information but not change it.
Read-Only Access concept
Read-only access lets someone view information but not change, create, or delete it.
real-world attacks concept
Real-world attacks are actual attempts to break into, damage, or abuse systems outside of a lab or classroom setting.
REALITY protocol protocol
REALITY is a traffic-obfuscation protocol used with Xray proxies to make connections resemble normal encrypted website traffic.
also: REALITY
Reboot concept
A reboot means restarting a computer, phone, server, or other device.
Received headers concept
Email header fields that record the servers and route a message took before reaching its recipient.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
recovery phrase concept
A recovery phrase is a list of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet if the device or app is lost.
recovery phrases concept
Recovery phrases are lists of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet or other secured account.
Red Menshen malware
Red Menshen is a malware family referenced in security reporting, associated with stealthy backdoor access to targeted systems.
Red team concept
The offensive security team that simulates real-world attacks to test an organization's defenses and improve security.
red teaming technique
Red teaming is an authorized exercise where security experts act like attackers to test an organization's defenses.
redact technique
To redact is to hide or remove sensitive information from text, logs, or documents before sharing them.
Redaction technique
Redaction is the process of hiding or removing sensitive information before sharing or storing data.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
Redirected technique
Sent automatically from one website address or page to another.
Redirector concept
A link, web page, or service that automatically sends a visitor to another web address.
redirects concept
Redirects are instructions that automatically send a user or browser from one web address to another.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
registry value concept
A named setting in the Windows Registry that stores configuration information for Windows or installed software.
regulated data concept
Information subject to legal or industry rules about how it must be stored, processed, or shared.
regulators organization
Regulators are government or official bodies that create and enforce rules for industries and organizations.
Rehearsal tool
Rehearsal is a browser-based AI agent that can navigate websites and perform tasks in the Token platform.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
also: Japanese relay, mail relay
remediate concept
To remediate means to fix a security problem or reduce the risk it creates.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
Remediation Guidance concept
Remediation guidance is advice on how to fix or reduce the risk from a security problem.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
remote access sessions concept
Connections that allow a user to control a computer from a different location, like via RDP or SSH.
remote access software concept
Software that allows a user to control a computer from a remote location, often abused by scammers and attackers to gain unauthorized access.
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
also: RAT
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.
Remote code execution (RCE) technique
A vulnerability or attack outcome that lets someone run commands or programs on another computer from afar.
also: RCE, RCE via file repository upload path traversal
Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities concept
Flaws that can let an attacker run their own commands or programs on another system.
Remote Connection concept
A remote connection lets someone access or support a computer or network from another location.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
Remote Desktop concept
A technology that lets you see and control a computer's desktop from another device over a network.
remote desktop services tool
Remote desktop services let someone view and control a computer over a network as if sitting in front of it.
also: RDS
Remote management concept
Remote management is controlling or configuring a computer, server, or device from another location over a network.
Remote script technique
A remote script is code downloaded or run from another system, often used for administration but risky if untrusted.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
also: remote code execution vulnerability
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
remotely exploitable concept
Able to be attacked over a network without the attacker needing physical access to the affected system.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
reputation checks technique
Reputation checks judge whether a sender, website, file, or service seems trustworthy based on past behavior and known risk signals.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Response Guidance concept
Advice that helps people decide what actions to take after a security incident or alert.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
Restricted resources concept
Restricted resources are files, systems, functions, or data that only authorized users should be able to access.
Retesting technique
Checking a previously reported security issue again to confirm that a fix works.
Retries concept
Repeated attempts by software to complete an operation after an earlier attempt failed.
Return-Path protocol
Return-Path is an email header that identifies where bounce messages should be sent.
reverse shell technique
A reverse shell is a technique where a compromised computer connects back to an attacker and gives them a command-line session.
Reverse Shells technique
A remote command connection in which an infected computer calls back to an attacker's system for instructions.
Reverse-Pivot Technique technique
A technique in which an attacker uses a compromised system to reach back toward another connected system, such as a technician's computer.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
Revoke technique
To cancel a credential, permission, or access key so it can no longer be used.
Role-Based Access technique
A method of granting permissions according to a person's job role rather than assigning each permission individually.
romania
Romania is a European country that may appear in cybersecurity reporting as a location, target, or law-enforcement partner.
root shell concept
A root shell is a command-line session with the highest administrator privileges on a Unix or Linux system.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
rootkit malware
A rootkit is malware designed to hide itself and give an attacker deep control over a computer.
Roundcube product
Roundcube is an open-source webmail application used to access email through a web browser.
RSA concept
RSA is a widely used public-key cryptography method for encryption and digital signatures.
RSA keys concept
RSA keys are cryptographic keys used to prove identity or protect data through encryption and digital signatures.
RSA private key concept
An RSA private key is a secret cryptographic file used to prove identity or decrypt data protected with RSA encryption.
rubygems
RubyGems is the package manager and public package repository for the Ruby programming language.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
run-command tool
run-command is a command or feature name for remotely executing commands on managed systems.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Rust Backdoor malware
Rust Backdoor is backdoor malware written in the Rust programming language that can give attackers hidden access to a compromised system.
Rust-based concept
Rust-based means software was written using the Rust programming language, which is known for speed and memory safety.
S3 product
S3 is Amazon’s cloud object-storage service, often used to store files, backups, logs, and website data.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
same-origin concept
Same-origin is a browser security rule that treats pages as related only when their protocol, domain, and port match.
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
sandbox-escape technique
A technique where malware breaks out of a restricted, isolated testing environment to attack the real underlying system.
sandboxed concept
Sandboxed means running software in a restricted environment so it has limited access to the rest of the system.
Sandboxed Cross-Origin Frame concept
A sandboxed cross-origin frame is an embedded webpage from another site that a browser restricts to reduce what it can do.
also: sandboxed cross-origin frames, same-origin context
sandboxing technique
Sandboxing means running a file or program in an isolated environment so it can be observed safely without risking the real system.
Saved Credentials concept
Saved credentials are passwords, tokens, or other login details stored by software for later use.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scanning activity technique
Scanning activity is probing systems or networks to find open services, devices, or weaknesses.
scareware malware
Software or web content that uses frightening fake warnings to pressure people into taking an unwanted action.
scheduled task technique
A scheduled task is a job set to run automatically at a certain time or under certain conditions.
scheduled-tasks
Scheduled tasks are automated jobs on a computer that attackers can abuse to run malware at specific times or after reboot.
scheduler.exe tool
scheduler.exe is an executable program file name that may refer to a task-scheduling or similarly named process.
SCL=-1 concept
SCL=-1 is a Microsoft email spam score value that usually means a message is treated as trusted and bypasses normal spam filtering.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
Scope Sentry tool
A security tool for discovering an organization's assets and internet-exposed systems.
Scoring concept
Scoring is the practice of assigning a number or rating to show how risky, important, or suspicious something is.
screenconnect
ScreenConnect, now ConnectWise Control, is a remote-support tool that attackers sometimes abuse for unauthorized access.
screenconnect-run-command tool
A tool or script associated with running commands through ScreenConnect remote-access software.
screenshot concept
A screenshot is a captured image of what is shown on a screen.
Secrets Manager product
Secrets Manager usually refers to a cloud service for storing and rotating sensitive values such as passwords, tokens, and API keys.
Secure Registry product
Secure Registry is a security-related product or service name referenced in reporting.
Security alerts concept
Security alerts are warnings from tools or services that something suspicious or risky may be happening.
security checks technique
Security checks are tests or reviews used to find risks, weaknesses, or unsafe behavior in a system.
Security flaws concept
Weaknesses or mistakes in software or systems that attackers may be able to exploit.
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
Security Management concept
Security Management is the process or product area for configuring, monitoring, and enforcing security controls.
Security policy concept
A security policy is a rule or set of rules that defines how systems, users, or data should be protected.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
security researchers organization
Security researchers are people who study systems, software, and attacks to find vulnerabilities and improve defenses.
security software product
Security software is software designed to protect computers, networks, or data from threats.
Security Systems concept
Security systems are tools and processes used to protect computers, networks, and information.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security tools tool
Security tools are software or hardware products used to detect, prevent, investigate, or respond to cyber threats.
Security Update concept
A software update that fixes vulnerabilities or other security-related problems.
also: update, updates, waiting update
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
also: recent updates, Windows security update
Security Warnings concept
Alerts that tell users about a possible security risk or unsafe action.
SEGA organization
A Japanese video-game and entertainment company.
Self Service+ product
Self Service+ is a product that lets employees handle some common technology tasks without waiting for IT support.
self-managed instances concept
Self-managed instances are software installations that an organization operates on its own servers or cloud accounts.
SendCommand tool
SendCommand is an AWS Systems Manager feature that remotely runs commands on managed computers.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive actions concept
Sensitive actions are operations that could significantly affect a person's data, money, accounts, privacy, or device and therefore should require extra approval.
Sensitive Configuration Information concept
Sensitive configuration information is private system setup data, such as account details, network settings, or security secrets, that should not be exposed.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
Sensitive details concept
Sensitive details are private pieces of information, such as passwords, bank numbers, or identity information, that should not be shared freely.
sensitive files concept
Sensitive files are files that contain private, secret, or valuable information that should not be exposed to unauthorized people.
sensitive government information concept
Sensitive government information is official data that could cause harm if exposed, such as security, personal, or operational details.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
Server Core product
Server Core is a minimal-installation option for Windows Server that has no traditional full desktop interface.
SERVER-DB01 product
A hostname used to identify a database server on a network.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) technique
A vulnerability that tricks a server into making network requests chosen by an attacker, often to internal services.
also: Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation
Server-side validation technique
A security check performed by an application's server to verify that submitted data or a token is legitimate.
server-side-request-forgery vulnerability
Server-side request forgery is a vulnerability that lets an attacker make a server send requests to places the attacker should not be able to reach directly.
service account concept
A non-human account used by an application or service to perform automated tasks, often holding elevated privileges.
service fingerprint technique
A service fingerprint is a set of visible clues that helps identify what software or service is running on a network system.
Service Outage concept
A service outage is a period when a system, website, or service is unavailable or not working properly.
service provider organization
A service provider is a company or organization that delivers a service, such as hosting, software, payments, or IT support, to customers.
service providers organization
Service providers are companies or organizations that deliver services such as internet access, hosting, software platforms, or managed IT support.
Service-Import Functionality concept
A software feature that brings service settings or data into a system from another source.
also: service import schema validation
Session cookies concept
Session cookies are small browser-stored values that help websites remember a logged-in user during a visit.
session hijacking technique
Session hijacking is when an attacker steals or takes over a user’s logged-in web session so they can act as that user.
Setup concept
The process of preparing a device, application, or account for use.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
Severity Score concept
A severity score is a rating that helps show how serious a security flaw or incident is.
severity scores concept
Severity scores rate how serious a vulnerability or security finding is.
Shadowserver organization
Shadowserver is an internet security watchdog group that tracks exposed systems and other security data.
shared credentials concept
Shared credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used by more than one person or system.
SharePoint Server product
SharePoint Server is Microsoft’s on-premises collaboration and document-management platform for organizations.
sharphound
SharpHound is a data collector for BloodHound that maps Active Directory relationships and attack paths.
shell history concept
Shell history is the saved list of commands a user typed in a command-line terminal.
Sign-In concept
Sign-in is the process of proving your identity to access a computer, account, or online service.
Signed Delivery Receipts concept
Signed delivery receipts are records confirming that a shipment was received, usually with a recipient's signature.
Signed requests technique
Signed requests are web or API requests that include cryptographic proof of who sent them and that they were not altered.
Signed-in session concept
The temporary state that keeps a user logged in to a website or application.
signing technique
A cryptographic process that uses a private key to prove that data came from its owner and was not changed.
Signing keys concept
Signing keys are cryptographic keys used to prove that software or data really came from a trusted publisher and was not changed.
Silent Lynx threat-actor
Silent Lynx is a threat-actor group linked to cyberespionage campaigns against organizations in Central Asia and the CIS region.
singapore
Singapore is a Southeast Asian country and technology hub often referenced in cybersecurity reporting.
SIS product
A software component referenced in security reporting.
Slab other
Slab is a named site or service referenced in security reporting.
slack
Slack is a workplace messaging and collaboration platform.
SMS messages protocol
SMS messages are ordinary text messages sent between mobile phones.
SMTP protocol
SMTP is the standard internet protocol used to send email between mail servers.
Sn00py malware
Sn00py is ransomware, a type of malware that encrypts files and demands payment to restore access.
also: Sn00py family, ransomware Trojan
Snaffler tool
Snaffler is a security tool used to find sensitive files on Windows network shares.
Snake threat-actor
A name used for the Turla threat actor and associated malware operations.
Snapchat product
Snapchat is a messaging and social media app used to share photos and videos.
Snort tool
Snort is an open-source network intrusion detection and prevention tool used to spot suspicious traffic.
also: Snort ruleset, Snort Subscriber Ruleset
Snort 2 tool
Snort 2 is a major version of the Snort open-source network intrusion detection and prevention system.
Snort 3 tool
Snort 3 is a major version of the Snort open-source network intrusion detection and prevention system.
Snort.org organization
Snort.org is the official website for Snort, an open-source network intrusion detection and prevention system.
SOAP Endpoints protocol
SOAP endpoints are network addresses where applications accept requests using the SOAP web-service messaging protocol.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
Social Security numbers concept
Social Security numbers are U.S. government identification numbers often targeted by criminals because they can be used for fraud.
also: SSNs
software development concept
Software development is the process of designing, writing, testing, and maintaining computer programs.
software vulnerability vulnerability
A software vulnerability is a flaw in code that attackers may be able to exploit.
Source concept
Source is a generic term for where information, code, or data comes from.
also: Source (WHERE)
Source Attribution concept
Source attribution is the process of identifying where a software package, action, or request originally came from.
source code concept
The human-readable code written by programmers that makes up software.
source IP concept
A source IP is the internet address a network request appears to come from.
source IP address concept
A source IP address is the network address a connection or message comes from.
source maps concept
Source maps are files that connect minified or bundled code back to the original source code, which can help debugging but may expose details to attackers.
south-africa other
South Africa is a country that may be mentioned as a location or target in a security story.
south-korea
South Korea is an East Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, espionage, or regional threats.
southeast-asia other
Southeast Asia is a region of Asia often referenced when describing where cyber activity or victims are located.
SpaceXSI organization
SpaceXSI is an organization or service provider referenced in security reporting.
spain other
Spain is a country in southwestern Europe.
spearphishing-link
A spearphishing link is a targeted phishing message that includes a malicious link tailored to a specific person or organization.
also: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
specially crafted message file technique
A message file deliberately formed to trigger a flaw when an application opens it.
Specially Crafted Packet technique
A network data packet deliberately formed to trigger a specific behavior or exploit a software weakness.
SPF protocol
SPF is an email check that verifies whether a sending server is allowed to send email for a domain.
also: spf=softfail
Spoofing technique
Spoofing is pretending to be someone or something trusted, such as an email sender, website, or device.
spoofing vulnerability vulnerability
A security flaw that can allow an attacker to pretend to be a trusted person, system, or website.
SQL Server product
SQL Server is Microsoft’s database product for storing, querying, and managing structured data.
SSL credential sets concept
SSL credential sets are collections of certificates and private keys used to prove a server's identity and encrypt connections.
ssrf vulnerability
A type of web vulnerability where an attacker tricks a server into making unintended requests to internal systems or external sites.
staging technique
Staging is the act of preparing data, tools, or files in an intermediate location before they are used, moved, or stolen.
staging environments concept
Non-production systems used to test software and changes before they are released to live users.
staging servers concept
Temporary or intermediary servers used to prepare, test, relay, or deliver content.
also: staging server, non-production
Startup concept
Startup usually refers to programs or scripts configured to run automatically when a computer or user session starts.
state-linked concept
State-linked describes activity believed to be connected to or supported by a national government.
stepsecurity organization
StepSecurity is a cybersecurity company focused on protecting software supply chains and CI/CD pipelines.
StepSecurity Secure Registry product
StepSecurity Secure Registry is a software package registry security tool or service referenced in supply-chain security reporting.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen accounts concept
User accounts that have been taken over by attackers, often through credential theft or phishing.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
stolen keys concept
Stolen keys are secret digital credentials, such as API keys or encryption keys, that attackers have taken and can use to access systems.
Stored concept
Stored is a ZIP entry type in which file data is saved without compression.
Stored cross-site scripting vulnerability
Stored cross-site scripting is a web vulnerability where malicious script is saved on a site and later runs in visitors' browsers.
also: MMS3 stored XSS
Stored passwords concept
Stored passwords are saved login credentials kept in a browser, application, password manager, or system.
Stored XSS vulnerability
Stored XSS is a web attack where malicious script is saved on a site and later runs in other users' browsers.
also: Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context), cross-site scripting (XSS)
Strict concept
A security setting that applies stronger restrictions to reduce the chance of unauthorized access.
Subdomains concept
Subdomains are parts of a domain name, such as blog.example.com, that can point to separate websites or services.
SUPER_ADMIN Accounts concept
SUPER_ADMIN accounts are highly privileged accounts that can usually manage nearly all settings, users, and data in a system.
supply chain concept
A supply chain is the network of vendors, software, services, and processes an organization depends on to operate.
surveillance concept
The act of monitoring people or activities, often covertly, as part of espionage, law enforcement, or malware functions like keyloggers.
suspicious activity concept
Suspicious activity is behavior that looks unusual or risky and may indicate fraud, hacking, or policy violations.
Symbiote malware
Symbiote is a Linux malware family that hides malicious activity by loading itself into other programs.
SYN protocol
A TCP packet flag used to begin the process of setting up a network connection.
Synacktiv organization
Synacktiv is a cybersecurity company known for security research, penetration testing, and vulnerability analysis.
Synchronization concept
Synchronization is the process of keeping data or systems matched and up to date across devices or services.
Synthetic Test Data concept
Artificially created data used to test systems without relying on real user information.
syslog-ng product
syslog-ng is software that collects, processes, and forwards system log messages.
System Event concept
A system event is a recorded action or status change from an operating system, device, or service.
system identity private key concept
A system identity private key is a secret cryptographic key a system uses to prove its identity to other systems.
System information concept
System information is basic detail about a computer, such as its operating system, hardware, username, and network settings.
System Settings product
System Settings is the macOS app where users change device, privacy, network, and security settings.
taiwan other
Taiwan is a territory in East Asia that is often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regional targeting or geopolitical activity.
Take Control product
Take Control is a remote access and support product used by IT teams to connect to customer devices.
Take Control of Accounts technique
Taking control of accounts means gaining unauthorized access to another person's online account and being able to act as that person.
TAKEOVER technique
TAKEOVER is a named account-control or exploitation step referenced in security reporting.
TCP protocol
TCP is a core internet protocol that reliably sends data between computers by establishing a connection.
TeamsAPK malware
TeamsAPK is a named malicious software or campaign reference in security reporting.
teamviewer
